</p><p>On July 29, 2025, Nvidia ordered 300,000 H20 AI chips from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) due to strong demand from Chinese tech firms like Tencent and Alibaba.<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_155-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters-155"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In August 2025, Nvidia and competitor <a href="/wiki/AMD" title="AMD">Advanced Micro Devices</a> agreed to pay 15% of the revenues from certain chip sales in China as part of an arrangement to obtain export licenses.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia will pay only for sales of the H20 chips.<sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>156<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 17, 2025, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said he was “disappointed” after the <a href="/wiki/Cyberspace_Administration_of_China" title="Cyberspace Administration of China">Cyberspace Administration of China</a> (CAC) ordered companies including TikTok parent company <a href="/wiki/ByteDance" title="ByteDance">ByteDance</a> and <a href="/wiki/Alibaba_Group" title="Alibaba Group">Alibaba</a> not to purchase the RTX Pro 6000D, a graphics chip made specifically for the Chinese market. China's internet regulator banned the country's largest technology companies from buying Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips as part of efforts to strengthen the domestic industry and compete with the United States. The CAC instructed companies this week to end both testing and orders of the RTX Pro 6000D, which Nvidia had designed as a tailor-made product for China, according to three people with knowledge of the matter.<sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>157<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 18, 2025, Nvidia announced it would invest $5 billion in <a href="/wiki/Intel" title="Intel">Intel</a>, backing the struggling U.S. chipmaker just weeks after the <a href="/wiki/White_House" title="White House">White House</a> arranged a deal for the federal government to take a major stake in the company. The investment will give Nvidia an immediate holding of about 4% in Intel once new shares are issued to finalize the agreement. Nvidia's move provides Intel with fresh support following years of unsuccessful turnaround efforts and will allow Nvidia to offer its powerful GB300 data center servers based on Blackwell GPUs on Intel's X86 architecture.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 22, 2025, Nvidia and <a href="/wiki/OpenAI" title="OpenAI">OpenAI</a> announced a memorandum of understanding for a partnership wherein Nvidia would invest $100 billion into OpenAI, and OpenAI would use Nvidia chips and systems in new data centers. OpenAI will build new AI data centers using Nvidia systems, amounting to at least 10 gigawatts system power, which is the equivalent of energy produced by more than four <a href="/wiki/Hoover_Dam" title="Hoover Dam">Hoover Dams</a>. The deal was meant to be a circular arrangement where OpenAI will pay back Nvidia's investment through the purchase of Nvidia's chips, which is a model common in AI partnerships.<sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>160<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This "circularity" is estimated at $35 billion in new Nvidia chips bought by OpenAI, for every $10 billion Nvidia invests in OpenAI.<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> As of January 2026, negotiations had not progressed beyond early stages, and the two companies were rethinking the partnership's structure. In the months leading up to this, chief executive Jensen Huang privately emphasized to industry associates that the original deal was non-binding and not finalized when announced.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In October 2025, a coalition of Nvidia, nonprofit <a href="/wiki/Electric_Power_Research_Institute" title="Electric Power Research Institute">Electric Power Research Institute</a> and <a href="/wiki/PJM_Interconnection" title="PJM Interconnection">PJM Interconnection</a> announced that the first commercial application of software—developed by startup Emerald AI (in which Nvidia invests), that adjusts the energy draw on a power grid in real time was to be deployed at a new data center under construction in <a href="/wiki/Virginia" title="Virginia">Virginia</a>. Dubbed "Aurora", the facility is expected to set a new flexible power standard.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>163<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>A server farm dedicated to autonomous AI was also announced in October 2025, as a collaboration between SDS Schönfeld, a data services firm owned by UC Schönfeld, and <a href="/wiki/VAST_Data" title="VAST Data">VAST Data</a>, an Israeli company specializing in AI storage management that collaborates closely with Nvidia. Reports indicate that approximately $30 billion has been secured for the <a href="/wiki/Bet_Yehoshua" class="mw-redirect" title="Bet Yehoshua">Bet Yehoshua</a> server farm. It is expected to feature "tens of petabytes of data infrastructure powered by VAST, along with thousands of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and Nvidia network processors."<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>164<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On October 29, 2025, Nvidia became the first company to reach a market capitalization of $5 trillion.<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia's stock prices fell by 2% on November 11, 2025, as the SoftBank Group dumped its entire Nvidia portfolio worth $5.8 billion, redirecting the capital towards OpenAI instead.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On December 1, 2025, Nvidia released Alpamayo-R1, an open source, vision-language-action AI model for self-driving vehicles. This was done so that developers and researchers can understand how these models work and come up with standard ways on how the industry can evaluate how they work.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On December 15, 2025, Nvidia announced the <a href="/wiki/Nemotron" title="Nemotron">Nemotron</a> 3 family of models consisting of Nano, Super and Ultra models, built on a hybrid mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture. Nvidia said Nano has around 30&nbsp;billion parameters, Super 100&nbsp;billion, and Ultra 500&nbsp;billion.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On December 18, 2025, Nvidia announced plans to build a major new research and development campus in Kiryat Tivon, Israel, projected to employ more than 10,000 people and become one of the company's largest sites outside the United States. The 22-acre complex is scheduled to begin construction in 2027, with initial operations expected in 2031, and will include laboratories, green areas, and public facilities. The project reinforces Israel's role as Nvidia's principal international development hub in advanced AI and computing technologies.<sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2025, it was announced that Nvidia had acquired <a href="/wiki/SchedMD" title="SchedMD">SchedMD</a>, the company behind the open-source workload manager <a href="/wiki/Slurm_Workload_Manager" title="Slurm Workload Manager">Slurm</a>, as part of an effort to expand its AI and high-performance computing software capabilities. Nvidia stated that Slurm would remain open-source and vendor-neutral after the acquisition, with no financial terms disclosed.<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2025, <a href="/wiki/CNBC" title="CNBC">CNBC</a> reported Nvidia had agreed to buy assets from <a href="/wiki/Groq" title="Groq">Groq</a> for $20 billion in cash. The deal included a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Nvidia for Groq's inference technology. Several of Groq's senior leaders, including its CEO, also agreed to join Nvidia as part of the deal. While both companies said Groq would continue to operate as an individual company, the transaction drew criticism from several industry analysts as a tactic to avoid regulatory scrutiny.<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In late 2025, Nvidia entered advanced negotiations to acquire <a href="/wiki/AI21_Labs" title="AI21 Labs">AI21 Labs</a>, an Israeli developer of large language models,<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in a deal valued at as much as $2 billion to $3 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The proposed transaction is widely described as a talent-focused "acquihire" aimed at integrating AI21's workforce of approximately 200 specialists into Nvidia's global artificial intelligence operations.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> If completed, the transaction would be Nvidia's second-largest Israeli acquisition after its $7 billion purchase of <a href="/wiki/Mellanox_Technologies" title="Mellanox Technologies">Mellanox</a> in 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>At <a href="/wiki/Consumer_Electronics_Show" title="Consumer Electronics Show">CES</a> 2026, CEO Jensen Huang unveiled Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI platform and the Alpamayo open-source model.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Hesai_Technology" title="Hesai Technology">Hesai</a> was also picked as Nvidia's laser technology partner, supplying Lidar sensors to the company, streamlining software, hardware, and data in its autonomous driving products.<sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In January 2026, Nvidia launched a new weather forecasting service called Earth-2. It is an open-sourced platform that can be incorporated to improve the AI function across models used by scientists, businesses and local governments.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On February 24, 2026, Nvidia announced its acquisition of Israeli startup Illumex, a developer of generative semantic data infrastructure, in a deal reportedly valued at around $60 million.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On 11 March 2026, Nvidia announced that it will invest $2 billion in artificial intelligence cloud company <a href="/wiki/Nebius_Group" title="Nebius Group">Nebius</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In April 2026, Nvidia announced the release of a new group of open-source artificial intelligence models designed specifically for quantum computing. The development caused a noticeable market surge for allied quantum computing companies.<sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> During the same month, Nvidia's market momentum was further bolstered by its primary manufacturing partner, TSMC, which reported a 35.1% year-on-year revenue increase for the first quarter of 2026, largely driven by robust global demand for AI accelerators.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>At the GTC conference in March 2026, Nvidia announced the "Vera Rubin" platform, the successor to its Blackwell architecture. The platform includes the Rubin GPU and Vera CPU, designed to scale "agentic AI" and offering significant performance improvements in large-scale AI factories.<sup id="cite_ref-NVIDIA_VeraRubin_186-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NVIDIA_VeraRubin-186"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In May 2026, Nvidia announced that it would be partnering with <a href="/wiki/Corning_Inc." title="Corning Inc.">Corning</a> and investing up to 3.2 billion to build 3 new advanced manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas as part of a optical fiber deal.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Leadership">Leadership</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=11" title="Edit section: Leadership"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Nvidia's key management as of March 2024 consists of:<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>188<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Board_of_directors">Board of directors</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=12" title="Edit section: Board of directors"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<p>For the fiscal year 2020, Nvidia reported earnings of US$2.796 billion, with an annual revenue of US$10.918 billion, a decline of 6.8% over the previous fiscal cycle. Nvidia's shares traded at over $531 per share, and its market capitalization was valued at over US$328.7 billion in January 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_194-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-194"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>For the Q2 of 2020, Nvidia reported sales of $3.87 billion, which was a 50% rise from the same period in 2019. The surge in sales was driven by people's higher demand for computer technology. According to the financial chief of the company, Colette Kress, the effects of the pandemic will "likely reflect this evolution in enterprise workforce trends with a greater focus on technologies, such as Nvidia laptops and virtual workstations, that enable remote work and virtual collaboration."<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2023, Nvidia crossed $1 trillion in market valuation during trading hours,<sup id="cite_ref-CNBC_5-30-2023_196-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNBC_5-30-2023-196"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and grew to $1.2 trillion by the following November.<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Ownership">Ownership</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=14" title="Edit section: Ownership"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The 10 largest shareholders of Nvidia in early 2026 were:<sup id="cite_ref-sws-ownership_198-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sws-ownership-198"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Fabrication">Fabrication</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=15" title="Edit section: Fabrication"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Nvidia <a href="/wiki/Fabless_manufacturing" title="Fabless manufacturing">uses external suppliers for all phases of manufacturing</a>, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Nvidia thus avoids most of the investment and production costs and risks associated with chip manufacturing, although it does sometimes directly procure some components and materials used in the production of its products (e.g., memory and substrates). Nvidia focuses its own resources on product design, quality assurance, marketing, and customer support.<sup id="cite_ref-annualreview2_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-annualreview2-199"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>198<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-valuechain2_200-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-valuechain2-200"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>199<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="GPU_Technology_Conference">GPU Technology Conference</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=16" title="Edit section: GPU Technology Conference"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1353705441">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+span.mw-empty-elt+.hatnote,.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_GTC" title="Nvidia GTC">Nvidia GTC</a></div>
<p>Nvidia's GPU Technology Conference (GTC) is a series of technical conferences held around the world.<sup id="cite_ref-GPU_Technology_Conference_201-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GPU_Technology_Conference-201"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>200<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It originated in 2009 in San Jose, California, with an initial focus on the potential for solving computing challenges through GPUs.<sup id="cite_ref-timeline_25-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-timeline-25"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In recent years,<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers"><span title="The time period mentioned near this tag is ambiguous. (June 2025)">when?</span></a></i>]</sup> the conference's focus has shifted to various applications of artificial intelligence and <a href="/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning">deep learning</a>; including <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_car" class="mw-redirect" title="Autonomous car">self-driving cars</a>, healthcare, <a href="/wiki/High_Performance_Computing" class="mw-redirect" title="High Performance Computing">high-performance computing</a>, and Nvidia Deep Learning Institute (DLI) training.<sup id="cite_ref-202" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-202"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>201<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> GTC 2018 attracted over 8400 attendees.<sup id="cite_ref-GPU_Technology_Conference_201-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GPU_Technology_Conference-201"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>200<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> GTC 2020 was converted to a digital event and drew roughly 59,000 registrants.<sup id="cite_ref-203" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-203"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>202<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> After several years of remote-only events, GTC in March 2024 returned to an in-person format in San Jose, California.<sup id="cite_ref-204" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-204"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>203<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>At GTC 2025, Nvidia unveiled its next-generation AI hardware, the Blackwell Ultra and Vera Rubin chips, signalling a leap toward <a href="/wiki/Agentic_AI" class="mw-redirect" title="Agentic AI">agentic AI</a> and <a href="/wiki/Reasoning_AI" class="mw-redirect" title="Reasoning AI">reasoning-capable computing</a>. Huang projected that AI-driven infrastructure would drive Nvidia's data center revenue to $1 trillion by 2028. The announcement also introduced Isaac GR00T N1 (humanoid robotics model), Cosmos (<a href="/wiki/Synthetic_training_data" class="mw-redirect" title="Synthetic training data">synthetic training data</a> AI), and the Newton physics engine, developed in collaboration with DeepMind and Disney Research.<sup id="cite_ref-205" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-205"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>204<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Product_families">Product families</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=17" title="Edit section: Product families"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:NVIDIA_Shield_Tablet_with_Wireless_Controller_(16131034479).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/NVIDIA_Shield_Tablet_with_Wireless_Controller_%2816131034479%29.jpg/250px-NVIDIA_Shield_Tablet_with_Wireless_Controller_%2816131034479%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/NVIDIA_Shield_Tablet_with_Wireless_Controller_%2816131034479%29.jpg/500px-NVIDIA_Shield_Tablet_with_Wireless_Controller_%2816131034479%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456"></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Shield_Tablet" class="mw-redirect" title="Shield Tablet">Shield Tablet</a> with its accompanying input pen (left) and <a href="/wiki/Gamepad" title="Gamepad">gamepad</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Nvidia's product families include graphics processing units, wireless communication devices, and automotive hardware and software, such as:
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/GeForce" title="GeForce">GeForce</a>, consumer-oriented graphics processing products</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_RTX" title="Nvidia RTX">RTX</a>, professional visual computing graphics processing products (replacing GTX and <a href="/wiki/Quadro" title="Quadro">Quadro</a>)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Quadro#For_business_NVS" class="mw-redirect" title="Nvidia Quadro">NVS</a>, a multi-display business graphics processor</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Tegra" title="Tegra">Tegra</a>, a <a href="/wiki/System_on_a_chip" title="System on a chip">system on a chip</a> series for mobile devices</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Tesla" title="Nvidia Tesla">Tesla</a>, line of dedicated general-purpose GPUs for high-end image generation applications in professional and scientific fields</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/NForce" title="NForce">nForce</a>, a motherboard chipset created by Nvidia for Intel (Celeron, Pentium and Core 2) and AMD (Athlon and Duron) microprocessors</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_GRID" title="Nvidia GRID">GRID</a>, a set of hardware and services by Nvidia for graphics virtualization</li>
<li>Shield, a range of gaming hardware including the <a href="/wiki/Shield_Portable" class="mw-redirect" title="Shield Portable">Shield Portable</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shield_Tablet" class="mw-redirect" title="Shield Tablet">Shield Tablet</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shield_TV" class="mw-redirect" title="Shield TV">Shield TV</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Drive" title="Nvidia Drive">Drive</a>, a range of hardware and software products for designers and manufacturers of autonomous vehicles. The <a href="/wiki/Drive_PX-series" class="mw-redirect" title="Drive PX-series">Drive PX-series</a> is a high-performance computer platform aimed at autonomous driving through deep learning,<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>205<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> while Driveworks is an operating system for <a href="/wiki/Self-driving_car" title="Self-driving car">driverless cars</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>206<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_BlueField" title="Nvidia BlueField">BlueField</a>, a range of <a href="/wiki/Data_processing_unit" title="Data processing unit">data processing units</a>, initially inherited from its acquisition of <a href="/wiki/Mellanox_Technologies" title="Mellanox Technologies">Mellanox Technologies</a><sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>207<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-209" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-209"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>208<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Datacenter/server class CPU, codenamed Grace, released in 2023<sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>209<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>210<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_DGX" title="Nvidia DGX">DGX</a>, an enterprise platform designed for deep learning applications</li>
<li>Maxine, a platform providing developers a suite of AI-based conferencing software<sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>211<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Omniverse" title="Nvidia Omniverse">Omniverse</a>, a platform for creating and operating <a href="/wiki/Metaverse" title="Metaverse">metaverse</a> applications<sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>212<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Open-source_software_support">Open-source software support</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=18" title="Edit section: Open-source software support"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Free_and_open-source_graphics_device_driver" title="Free and open-source graphics device driver">Free and open-source graphics device driver</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mesa_3D" class="mw-redirect" title="Mesa 3D">Mesa 3D</a>, and <a href="/wiki/OpenPOWER_Foundation" title="OpenPOWER Foundation">OpenPOWER Foundation</a></div>
<p>Until September 23, 2013, Nvidia had not published any documentation for its advanced hardware,<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>213<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> meaning that programmers could not write <a href="/wiki/Free_and_open-source" class="mw-redirect" title="Free and open-source">free and open-source</a> <a href="/wiki/Device_driver" title="Device driver">device drivers</a> for its products without resorting to <a href="/wiki/Reverse_engineering" title="Reverse engineering">reverse engineering</a>. Additionally, features like its compute platform <a href="/wiki/CUDA" title="CUDA">CUDA</a> and the <a href="/wiki/DLSS" class="mw-redirect" title="DLSS">DLSS</a> technology suite are proprietary and only available on its hardware. As such, Nvidia has been notable for proprietization and vendor-locking practices.
</p><p>Nvidia has released Linux &lt;open-source GPU kernel modules&gt; under dual GPL/MIT licensing, allowing developers to inspect the driver module code and contribute improvements in collaboration with the community.<a rel="nofollow" class="external autonumber" href="https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-releases-open-source-gpu-kernel-modules">[1]</a> The Nvidia <a href="https://github.com/NVIDIA/open-gpu-kernel-modules" class="extiw" title="github:NVIDIA/open-gpu-kernel-modules">open-gpu-kernel-modules repository</a> on <a href="/wiki/GitHub" title="GitHub">GitHub</a> provides the publicly accessible source code for these modules, supporting modern GPU architectures in Linux environments.<sup id="cite_ref-github_215-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-github-215"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>214<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Furthermore, Nvidia's acquisition of SchedMD and the release of new open-source AI models highlight its broader commitment to open-source software and the AI ecosystem.<a rel="nofollow" class="external autonumber" href="https://www.reuters.com/business/nvidia-buys-ai-software-provider-schedmd-expand-open-source-ai-push-2025-12-15/">[2]</a>
</p><p>Instead, Nvidia provides its own binary GeForce graphics drivers for <a href="/wiki/X.Org_Server" title="X.Org Server">X.Org</a> and an open-source library that interfaces with the <a href="/wiki/Linux_kernel" title="Linux kernel">Linux</a>, <a href="/wiki/FreeBSD" title="FreeBSD">FreeBSD</a> or <a href="/wiki/Solaris_(operating_system)" class="mw-redirect" title="Solaris (operating system)">Solaris</a> kernels and the proprietary graphics software. Nvidia also provided but stopped supporting an obfuscated open-source driver that only supports two-dimensional hardware acceleration and ships with the X.Org distribution.<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>215<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The proprietary nature of Nvidia's drivers has generated dissatisfaction within <a href="/wiki/Free_software_community" class="mw-redirect" title="Free software community">free-software communities</a>. In a 2012 talk, <a href="/wiki/Linus_Torvalds" title="Linus Torvalds">Linus Torvalds</a> gave <a href="/wiki/The_finger" title="The finger">a middle-finger gesture</a> and criticized Nvidia's stance toward Linux.<sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>216<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>217<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some Linux and BSD users insist on using only open-source drivers and regard Nvidia's insistence on providing nothing more than a binary-only driver as inadequate, given that competing manufacturers such as <a href="/wiki/Intel" title="Intel">Intel</a> offer support and documentation for <a href="/wiki/Open-source_model" class="mw-redirect" title="Open-source model">open-source</a> developers, and others like <a href="/wiki/Advanced_Micro_Devices" class="mw-redirect" title="Advanced Micro Devices">AMD</a> release partial documentation and provide some active development.<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>218<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ubuntugamer_220-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ubuntugamer-220"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>219<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia only provides x86/x64 and ARMv7-A versions of its proprietary driver; as a result, features like <a href="/wiki/CUDA" title="CUDA">CUDA</a> are unavailable on other platforms.<sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>220<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some users claim that Nvidia's Linux drivers impose artificial restrictions, like limiting the number of monitors that can be used at the same time, but the company has not commented on these accusations.<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>221<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2014, with its Maxwell GPUs, Nvidia started to require firmware by it to unlock all features of its graphics cards.<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>222<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>223<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>224<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On May 12, 2022, Nvidia announced that it is opensourcing its GPU kernel modules.<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>225<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>226<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-github_215-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-github-215"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>214<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Support for Nvidia's firmware was implemented in nouveau in 2023, which allows proper power management and GPU reclocking for Turing and newer graphics card generations.<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>227<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>228<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On July 21, 2025, Nvidia announced to extend CUDA support to <a href="/wiki/RISC-V" title="RISC-V">RISC-V</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>229<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>230<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>231<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>As of 2026, NVIDIA has over a 100 different open-source projects available on GitHub in different areas such as computer vision, networking, cybersecurity, AR/VR, Robotics, Generative AI etc<sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>232<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Nvidia_proprietary_software">Nvidia proprietary software</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=20" title="Edit section: Nvidia proprietary software"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Deep_learning">Deep learning</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=21" title="Edit section: Deep learning"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Nvidia GPUs are used in <a href="/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning">deep learning</a>, and accelerated analytics due to Nvidia's <a href="/wiki/CUDA" title="CUDA">CUDA</a> software platform and API which allows programmers to utilize the higher number of cores present in GPUs to <a href="/wiki/Parallel_computing" title="Parallel computing">parallelize</a> <a href="/wiki/BLAS" class="mw-redirect" title="BLAS">BLAS</a> operations which are extensively used in <a href="/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning">machine learning</a> algorithms.<sup id="cite_ref-Elsevier_12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Elsevier-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> They were included in many Tesla, Inc. vehicles before Musk announced at Tesla Autonomy Day in 2019 that the company developed its own SoC and full self-driving computer now and would stop using Nvidia hardware for their vehicles.<sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>235<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>236<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> These GPUs are used by researchers, laboratories, tech companies and enterprise companies.<sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>237<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2009, Nvidia was involved in what was called the "big bang" of deep learning, "as deep-learning neural networks were combined with Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs)".<sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>238<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> That year, the <a href="/wiki/Google_Brain" title="Google Brain">Google Brain</a> team used Nvidia GPUs to create <a href="/wiki/Deep_neural_networks" class="mw-redirect" title="Deep neural networks">deep neural networks</a> capable of machine learning, where <a href="/wiki/Andrew_Ng" title="Andrew Ng">Andrew Ng</a> determined that GPUs could increase the speed of deep learning systems by about 100 times.<sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>239<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="DGX">DGX</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=22" title="Edit section: DGX"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_DGX" title="Nvidia DGX">Nvidia DGX</a></div>
<p>DGX is a line of <a href="/wiki/Supercomputers" class="mw-redirect" title="Supercomputers">supercomputers</a> by Nvidia.
</p><p>In April 2016, Nvidia produced the <a href="/wiki/DGX-1" class="mw-redirect" title="DGX-1">DGX-1</a> based on an 8 GPU cluster, to improve the ability of users to use deep learning by combining GPUs with integrated deep learning software.<sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>240<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia gifted its first DGX-1 to <a href="/wiki/OpenAI" title="OpenAI">OpenAI</a> in August 2016 to help it train larger and more complex AI models with the capability of reducing processing time from six days to two hours.<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>241<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It also developed Nvidia Tesla K80 and P100 GPU-based virtual machines, which are available through <a href="/wiki/Google_Cloud_Platform" title="Google Cloud Platform">Google Cloud</a>, which Google installed in November 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>243<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Microsoft" title="Microsoft">Microsoft</a> added GPU servers in a preview offering of its N series based on Nvidia's Tesla K80s, each containing 4992 processing cores. Later that year, AWS's P2 instance was produced using up to 16 Nvidia Tesla K80 GPUs. That month Nvidia also partnered with IBM to create a software kit that boosts the AI capabilities of <a href="/wiki/Watson_(computer)" class="mw-redirect" title="Watson (computer)">Watson</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-245" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-245"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>244<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> called IBM PowerAI.<sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>245<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>246<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia also offers its own Nvidia Deep Learning software development kit.<sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>247<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2017, the GPUs were also brought online at the <a href="/wiki/Riken" title="Riken">Riken</a> Center for Advanced Intelligence Project for <a href="/wiki/Fujitsu" title="Fujitsu">Fujitsu</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>248<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company's deep learning technology led to a boost in its 2017 earnings.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>249<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2018, Nvidia researchers demonstrated imitation-learning techniques for industrial robots. They have created a system that, after a short revision and testing, can already be used to control the universal robots of the next generation. In addition to GPU manufacturing, Nvidia provides parallel processing capabilities to researchers and scientists that allow them to efficiently run high-performance applications.<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>250<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Robotics">Robotics</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=23" title="Edit section: Robotics"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In 2020, Nvidia unveiled "<a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Omniverse" title="Nvidia Omniverse">Omniverse</a>", a virtual environment designed for engineers.<sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia also open-sourced Isaac Sim, which makes use of this Omniverse to train robots through simulations that mimic the physics of the robots and the real world.<sup id="cite_ref-253" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-253"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>252<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>253<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2024, Huang oriented Nvidia's focus towards <a href="/wiki/Humanoid_robot" title="Humanoid robot">humanoid robots</a> and <a href="/wiki/Self-driving_car" title="Self-driving car">self-driving cars</a>, which he expects to gain widespread adoption.<sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>254<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>255<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2025, Nvidia announced Isaac GR00T N1, an open-source <a href="/wiki/Foundation_model" title="Foundation model">foundation model</a> "designed to expedite the development and capabilities of humanoid robots". <a href="/wiki/Neura_Robotics" title="Neura Robotics">Neura Robotics</a>, <a href="/wiki/1X_Technologies" title="1X Technologies">1X Technologies</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vention" title="Vention">Vention</a> are among the first companies to use the model.<sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>257<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-259" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-259"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>258<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Automotive">Automotive</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=24" title="Edit section: Automotive"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>NVIDIA has been involves in the automotive industry since introducing <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Drive" title="Nvidia Drive">NVIDIA drive</a> in CES 2015<sup id="cite_ref-260" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-260"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>259<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>.
</p><p>In April 2021, NVIDIA announced "DRIVE Sim" - A simulation platform for autonomous vehicles based on the <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Omniverse" title="Nvidia Omniverse">Omniverse</a> platform, which according to NVIDIA brought high fidelity, and was much more physically accurate and fully repeatable<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>260<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> which is required for <a href="/wiki/Verification_and_validation" title="Verification and validation">V&amp;V</a>.
</p><p>In January 2026, NVIDIA announced Alpamayo<sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>261<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>, "family of open AI models, simulation tools and datasets designed to accelerate the next era of safe, reasoning‑based autonomous vehicle (AV) development.".
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Inception_Program">Inception Program</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=25" title="Edit section: Inception Program"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Nvidia's Inception Program was created to support startups making exceptional advances in the fields of artificial intelligence and data science. Award winners are announced at Nvidia's GTC Conference. In May 2017, the program had 1,300 companies.<sup id="cite_ref-NVI15_263-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NVI15-263"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>262<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> As of March 2018, there were 2,800 startups in the Inception Program.<sup id="cite_ref-264" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-264"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>263<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> As of August 2021, the program has over 8,500 members in 90 countries, with cumulative funding of US$60 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-265" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-265"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>264<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Controversies">Controversies</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=26" title="Edit section: Controversies"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="GTX_970_hardware_specifications_advertising_dispute">GTX 970 hardware specifications advertising dispute</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=27" title="Edit section: GTX 970 hardware specifications advertising dispute"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/GeForce_900_series#Advertising_controversy" title="GeForce 900 series">GeForce 900 series §&nbsp;Advertising controversy</a></div>
<p>Issues with the GeForce GTX 970's specifications were first brought up by users when they found out that the cards, while featuring 4&nbsp;GB of memory, rarely accessed memory over the 3.5&nbsp;GB boundary. Further testing and investigation eventually led to Nvidia issuing a statement that the card's initially announced specifications had been altered without notice before the card was made commercially available, and that the card took a performance hit once memory over the 3.5&nbsp;GB limit were put into use.<sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>265<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>266<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>267<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The card's back-end hardware specifications, initially announced as being identical to those of the GeForce GTX 980, differed in the amount of L2 cache (1.75&nbsp;MB versus 2&nbsp;MB in the GeForce GTX 980) and the number of ROPs (56 versus 64 in the 980). Additionally, it was revealed that the card was designed to access its memory as a 3.5&nbsp;GB section, plus a 0.5&nbsp;GB one, access to the latter being 7 times slower than the first one.<sup id="cite_ref-269" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-269"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>268<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company then went on to promise a specific driver modification to alleviate the performance issues produced by the cutbacks suffered by the card.<sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>269<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> However, Nvidia later clarified that the promise had been a miscommunication and there would be no specific driver update for the GTX 970.<sup id="cite_ref-271" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-271"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>270<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia claimed that it would assist customers who wanted refunds in obtaining them.<sup id="cite_ref-272" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-272"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>271<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On February 26, 2015, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang went on record in Nvidia's official blog to apologize for the incident.<sup id="cite_ref-273" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-273"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>272<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In February 2015 a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising was filed against Nvidia and Gigabyte Technology in the <a href="/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_Northern_District_of_California" title="United States District Court for the Northern District of California">United States District Court for the Northern District of California</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-970lawsuit_274-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-970lawsuit-274"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>273<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-275" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-275"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>274<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia revealed that it is able to disable individual units, each containing 256&nbsp;KB of L2 cache and 8 ROPs, without disabling whole memory controllers.<sup id="cite_ref-AnandTechCorrectionPage2_276-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-276"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This comes at the cost of dividing the memory bus into high speed and low speed segments that cannot be accessed at the same time unless one segment is reading while the other segment is writing because the L2/ROP unit managing both of the GDDR5 controllers shares the read return channel and the write data bus between the two GDDR5 controllers and itself.<sup id="cite_ref-AnandTechCorrectionPage2_276-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-276"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This is used in the GeForce GTX 970, which therefore can be described as having 3.5 GB in its high speed segment on a 224-bit bus and 0.5 GB in a low speed segment on a 32-bit bus.<sup id="cite_ref-AnandTechCorrectionPage2_276-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-276"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On July 27, 2016, Nvidia agreed to a preliminary settlement of the U.S. class action lawsuit,<sup id="cite_ref-970lawsuit_274-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-970lawsuit-274"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>273<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> offering a $30 refund on GTX 970 purchases. The agreed upon refund represents the portion of the cost of the storage and performance capabilities the consumers assumed they were obtaining when they purchased the card.<sup id="cite_ref-277" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-277"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>276<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="GeForce_Partner_Program">GeForce Partner Program</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=28" title="Edit section: GeForce Partner Program"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/GeForce_Partner_Program" title="GeForce Partner Program">GeForce Partner Program</a></div>
<p>The Nvidia GeForce Partner Program was a <a href="/wiki/Marketing" title="Marketing">marketing</a> program designed to provide partnering companies with benefits such as public relations support, <a href="/wiki/Video_game_bundle" class="mw-redirect" title="Video game bundle">video game bundling</a>, and marketing development funds.<sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>277<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The program proved to be controversial, with complaints about it possibly being an <a href="/wiki/Anti-competitive" class="mw-redirect" title="Anti-competitive">anti-competitive</a> practice.<sup id="cite_ref-:02_279-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-279"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>278<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>First announced in a blog post on March 1, 2018,<sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>279<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> it was canceled on May 4, 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>280<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Hardware_Unboxed">Hardware Unboxed</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=29" title="Edit section: Hardware Unboxed"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>On December 10, 2020, Nvidia told <a href="/wiki/YouTube" title="YouTube">YouTube</a> tech reviewer Steven Walton of Hardware Unboxed that it would no longer supply him with GeForce Founders Edition graphics card review units.<sup id="cite_ref-282" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-282"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>281<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-283" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-283"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>282<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In a Twitter message, Hardware Unboxed said, "Nvidia have officially decided to ban us from receiving GeForce Founders Edition GPU review samples. Their reasoning is that we are focusing on rasterization instead of ray tracing. They have said they will revisit this 'should your editorial direction change.<span style="padding-right:.15em;">'</span>"<sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>283<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>
In emails that were disclosed by Walton from Nvidia Senior PR Manager Bryan Del Rizzo, Nvidia had said:</p><blockquote><p>...your GPU reviews and recommendations have continued to focus singularly on rasterization performance, and you have largely discounted all of the other technologies we offer gamers. It is very clear from your community commentary that you do not see things the same way that we, gamers, and the rest of the industry do.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_285-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-285"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></p></blockquote><p>TechSpot, partner site of Hardware Unboxed, said, "this and other related incidents raise serious questions around journalistic independence and what they are expecting of reviewers when they are sent products for an unbiased opinion."<sup id="cite_ref-:1_285-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-285"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>A number of technology reviewers came out strongly against Nvidia's move.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_286-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-286"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>285<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>286<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Linus_Sebastian" title="Linus Sebastian">Linus Sebastian</a>, of <a href="/wiki/Linus_Tech_Tips" class="mw-redirect" title="Linus Tech Tips">Linus Tech Tips</a>, titled the episode of his weekly WAN Show, "NVIDIA might ACTUALLY be EVIL..."<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>287<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and was highly critical of the company's move to dictate specific outcomes of technology reviews.<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>288<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The review site Gamers Nexus said it was, "Nvidia's latest decision to shoot both its feet: They've now made it so that any reviewers covering RT will become subject to scrutiny from untrusting viewers who will suspect subversion by the company. Shortsighted self-own from NVIDIA."<sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>289<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Two days later, Nvidia reversed its stance.<sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>290<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>291<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Hardware Unboxed sent out a Twitter message, "I just received an email from Nvidia apologizing for the previous email &amp; they've now walked everything back."<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>292<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:2_286-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-286"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>285<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On December 14, Hardware Unboxed released a video explaining the controversy from their viewpoint.<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>293<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Via Twitter, they also shared a second apology sent by Nvidia's Del Rizzo that said "to withhold samples because I didn't agree with your commentary is simply inexcusable and crossed the line."<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>294<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>295<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Improper_disclosures_about_cryptomining">Improper disclosures about cryptomining</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=30" title="Edit section: Improper disclosures about cryptomining"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In 2018, Nvidia's chips became popular for <a href="/wiki/Cryptomining" class="mw-redirect" title="Cryptomining">cryptomining</a>, the process of obtaining crypto rewards in exchange for verifying transactions on distributed ledgers, the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Securities_and_Exchange_Commission" title="United States Securities and Exchange Commission">United States Securities and Exchange Commission</a> (SEC) said. However, the company failed to disclose that it was a "significant element" of its revenue growth from sales of chips designed for gaming, the SEC further added in a statement and charging order. Those omissions misled investors and analysts who were interested in understanding the impact of cryptomining on Nvidia's business, the SEC emphasized. Nvidia, which did not admit or deny the findings, has agreed to pay $5.5 million to settle civil charges, according to a statement made by the SEC in May 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>296<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="French_Competition_Authority_Investigation">French Competition Authority Investigation</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=31" title="Edit section: French Competition Authority Investigation"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>On September 26, 2023, Nvidia's French offices were searched by the French Competition Authority. The raid, authorized by a judge, was part of an investigation into suspected anti-competitive practices in the graphics card sector. Nvidia has not publicly commented on the incident.<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>297<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Chinese_market_halt">Chinese market halt</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=32" title="Edit section: Chinese market halt"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In August 2025, Nvidia ordered suppliers to halt production of its H20 AI chip following Chinese government directives warning domestic companies against purchasing the processor due to security concerns.<sup id="cite_ref-reuters-h20-halt_299-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters-h20-halt-299"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>298<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-info-h20-halt_300-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-info-h20-halt-300"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>299<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company directed suppliers including <a href="/wiki/Taiwan_Semiconductor_Manufacturing_Company" class="mw-redirect" title="Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company">Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company</a>, Samsung Electronics, and <a href="/wiki/Amkor_Technology" title="Amkor Technology">Amkor Technology</a> to suspend work on the China-focused processor.<sup id="cite_ref-yahoo-h20-suppliers_301-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-yahoo-h20-suppliers-301"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>300<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The H20 was developed in late 2023 specifically for the Chinese market to comply with U.S. export restrictions, featuring 96GB of <a href="/wiki/HBM3" class="mw-redirect" title="HBM3">HBM3</a> memory and 4.0 TB/s memory bandwidth—higher than the H100—but with significantly reduced computational power at 296 <a href="/wiki/FLOPS" class="mw-redirect" title="FLOPS">TFLOPs</a> compared to the H100's 1979 TFLOPs.<sup id="cite_ref-futunn-h20-specs_302-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-futunn-h20-specs-302"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>301<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-binance-h20-performance_303-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-binance-h20-performance-303"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>302<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Despite lower raw performance, the H20 demonstrated over 20% faster performance than the H100 in <a href="/wiki/Large_language_model" title="Large language model">large language model</a> inference tasks due to architectural optimizations.<sup id="cite_ref-futunn-h20-specs_302-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-futunn-h20-specs-302"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>301<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-binance-h20-performance_303-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-binance-h20-performance-303"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>302<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Prior to the production halt, Nvidia had placed substantial orders for the H20, including 300,000 units from TSMC in July 2025, driven by strong demand from Chinese technology companies.<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_155-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters-155"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> CEO <a href="/wiki/Jensen_Huang" title="Jensen Huang">Jensen Huang</a> denied allegations that the H20 contained security backdoors, stating the chips were designed solely for commercial use.<sup id="cite_ref-ainvest-huang-backdoors_304-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ainvest-huang-backdoors-304"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>303<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The production suspension occurred as Nvidia was developing the B30A, a new chip based on its Blackwell architecture intended to succeed the H20 in the Chinese market.<sup id="cite_ref-reuters-b30a-chip_305-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters-b30a-chip-305"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>304<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Following prolonged negotiations, the United States announced in 2026 that it would permit the export of newer H200 chips to China under specified conditions. The move was expected to stimulate market activity. The Chinese market, estimated to be worth hundreds of billions and potentially trillions of U.S. dollars, presents significant profit opportunities for American firms, with revenues reinforcing U.S. leading positions.<sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>305<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>306<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The decision also drew criticism for simultaneously constraining and strengthening China's technological capabilities, and was described by some critics as unreasonable.<sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>307<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> However, some technology experts argue that China's development capacity has exceeded expectations and warn that the full ban policy could potentially enable real challenges to U.S. influence over technical standard setting.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>308<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>309<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> China quickly responded by imposing restrictions on certain foreign chips to be imported.<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>310<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Despite China's efforts to shape technical standards, still, American products and ecosystem retain strong appeal, raising government concerns over possible fragmentation and reduced reinvestment in their own artificial intelligence progress.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>311<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> More broadly, China is seen as seeking long-term influence to counterbalance the United States rather than maintaining competitive complementarity rival.<sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>312<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Data_scraping_&amp;_Anna's_Archive_piracy"><span id="Data_scraping_.26_Anna.27s_Archive_piracy"></span>Data scraping &amp; Anna's Archive piracy</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&amp;action=edit&amp;section=33" title="Edit section: Data scraping &amp; Anna's Archive piracy"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Anna%27s_Archive#Nvidia_lawsuit" title="Anna's Archive">Anna's Archive §&nbsp;Nvidia lawsuit</a></div>
<p>Nvidia has been involved in heavy data scraping for illegal AI model training. In 2024, internal conversations revealed that Nvidia was scraping large amounts of videos from YouTube without permission, and by circumventing protection measures.<sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>313<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In January 2026, a court filing revealed that Nvidia developers contacted shadow library <a href="/wiki/Anna%27s_Archive" title="Anna's Archive">Anna's Archive</a> to evaluate the use of <a href="/wiki/Online_piracy" title="Online piracy">pirated content</a> for model training, which management gave green light for despite legality concerns from the site.<sup id="cite_ref-315" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-315"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>314<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia denied the allegations and filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit.<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>315<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>316<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>317<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
